findings.name: ClusterRole grants nodes/proxy enabling Kubelet API RCE
findings.message: ClusterRole grants nodes/proxy access, enabling full Kubelet API (exec/run/attach) on all nodes

steps: Audit all ClusterRoles for nodes/proxy permissions
Remove nodes/proxy from ClusterRole rules unless strictly required
Implement network policies restricting pod access to port 10250
Deploy node-level runtime detection (Falco, Tetragon) for Kubelet connections
Consider deploying Kyverno policy restrict-clusterrole-nodesproxy as admission guard
Kyverno equivalents: KPOL-0279 and KPOL-0367
Monitor KEP-2862 progress for fine-grained Kubelet authorization (K8s 1.36+)
commands: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "nodes/proxy") | .metadata.name'
kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name == "<ROLE_NAME>") | {name: .metadata.name, subjects: .subjects}'

next_step.description: Audit all ClusterRoles for nodes/proxy permissions
next_step.command: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "nodes/proxy") | .metadata.name'

findings.message: ClusterRoleBinding grants nodes/proxy via ClusterRole "keda-operator" to ServiceAccount default/keda-operator

steps: Identify which subjects are bound to the nodes/proxy ClusterRole
Remove unnecessary bindings or switch to more restrictive ClusterRoles
Audit ServiceAccount usage to verify necessity
Restrict binding scope where possible
Related policy controls: KPOL-0279 and KPOL-0367
commands: kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.roleRef.name == "<ROLE_NAME>") | {name: .metadata.name, subjects: .subjects}'

findings.name: ClusterRole grants secrets read permissions
findings.message: ClusterRole grants secrets get/list, enabling credential exfiltration across namespaces

steps: Remove secrets get/list permissions from ClusterRoles that do not require credential access
Scope secret access to namespaced Role bindings where possible
commands: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(any(.rules[]?; any(.resources[]?; .=="secrets"))) | .metadata.name'

next_step.description: Remove secrets get/list permissions from ClusterRoles that do not require credential access
next_step.command: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(any(.rules[]?; any(.resources[]?; .=="secrets"))) | .metadata.name'

findings.name: ClusterRole uses wildcard resources with broad verbs
findings.message: ClusterRole uses wildcard resources with broad verbs, indicating overprivileged admin access

steps: Replace wildcard resources with explicit resource lists
Remove unnecessary broad verbs and keep least-privilege verbs only
commands: kubectl get clusterroles -o json | jq '.items[] | select(any(.rules[]?; any(.resources[]?; .=="*"))) | .metadata.name'

next_step.description: Replace wildcard resources with explicit resource lists
